categories.name: error return
references: git-cliff/src/main.rs:16 fn main() -> Result<()>; its ? operators at :26 (logger::init), :47 (list_templates), :55 (init_config_from), :64 (git_cliff::run) and :75 (File::create) return the error to the Rust runtime
git-cliff/src/main.rs:82-96: write_changelog Ok gives 0, Err is logged and gives 1, then process::exit(exit_code) at :96, the only explicit exit in the git-cliff and git-cliff-core sources
git-cliff/src/lib.rs:584 run and :909 write_changelog return Result; git2 0.21.0, tera 1.20.1 and reqwest errors reach main through ? as git_cliff_core::error::Error

rustc 1.98.1 (48a229ce) library/std/src/process.rs:2718-2727: an Err returned by main prints Error: {err:?} and reports ExitCode::FAILURE; library/std/src/sys/process/windows.rs:809 defines FAILURE as EXIT_FAILURE, 1
Cargo.toml [profile.release] and .github/workflows/cd.yml:162: the Windows asset is built with cargo build --release --locked --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and the default features
categories.finding: Every error git-cliff returns ends the process with status 1, through process::exit(1) or the runtime's report of the Err from main; success is 0. No path of the binary or core crates passes another value to process::exit or ExitCode.

categories.name: argument-parsing errors
references: git-cliff/src/main.rs:18 Opt::parse(), the clap derive parser of git-cliff/src/args.rs; git-cliff/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock: clap and clap_builder 4.6.6

clap v4.6.6 (4a622b43) clap_builder/src/derive.rs:31-41: Parser::parse calls get_matches, then Error::exit for a conversion error; clap_builder/src/builder/command.rs:689 and :765 call Error::exit on a parse error

clap_builder/src/error/mod.rs:233-249: exit_code is USAGE_CODE for an error printed on standard error and SUCCESS_CODE for help or version, and exit calls std::process::exit(self.exit_code()); clap_builder/src/util/mod.rs:26 SUCCESS_CODE = 0, :32 USAGE_CODE = 2
grep of clap_builder/src: std::process::exit appears only at error/mod.rs:248
git-cliff/src/lib.rs:707-711: a check after parsing (-o and -p naming the same file) returns Error::ArgumentError to main, status 1
categories.finding: An argument-parsing error exits 2, and --help or --version exits 0, through clap's Error::exit, the only process exit in clap_builder 4.6.6. Checks made after parsing return errors to main, status 1.

categories.name: propagated helper statuses
references: git-cliff-core/src/command.rs:11-53 run: a helper started with cmd /C that exits nonzero becomes IoError::other("command exited with {status:?}"), returned as an Err; the status is only formatted into the message
git-cliff-core/src/repo.rs:774 and :1056: the only other std::process::Command uses, both inside #[cfg(test)] mod test (repo.rs:772-773)
git-cliff/src/lib.rs:35-45 check_new_version (update-informer 1.3.0, a default feature) discards every error through .ok().flatten()
git-cliff/src/lib.rs:648-654: a remote configuration read through reqwest propagates its errors with ?
the bundle's cliff.toml starts no command helper: its one replace_command preprocessor line is a comment
categories.finding: No helper's status becomes git-cliff's exit status: a failing shell helper yields an error whose message holds the status, and main ends with 1. libgit2 runs in process and returns errors. The bundle's cliff.toml starts no helper.

categories.name: panics and abnormal termination
references: Cargo.toml:31-37 [profile.release] panic = "unwind"; the panic = "abort" of [profile.dev] (Cargo.toml:21-24) does not apply to the release build
rustc 1.98.1 (48a229ce) library/std/src/rt.rs:175-183: a panic of the main thread is caught and the program returns 101
grep of every .rs and .toml file: no panic::set_hook, catch_unwind or process::abort in git-cliff or git-cliff-core

git-cliff/src/lib.rs:720-721: .expect("Incorrect config value for 'sort_commits'") panics on an unknown sort_commits value; other main-thread unwrap calls at lib.rs:429, :454, :484, :497, :543-548 and logger.rs:126
git-cliff-core/src/command.rs:35-39: expect("Failed to write to stdin") runs in a spawned thread, whose panic ends that thread only

Windows: an abort (a panic while panicking) ends through __fastfail with 0xC0000409, a stack overflow with 0xC00000FD, an access violation with 0xC0000005, Ctrl+C with 0xC000013A; git-cliff has no console control handler (no ctrlc or signal-hook dependency)
categories.finding: A main-thread panic exits 101, and an abnormal termination exits with an NTSTATUS value of 0xC0000000 or more; neither is 69. The reachable panic at lib.rs:721 was observed with status 101.
